summary: C reaches steed.c:landing_spot when a monster knocks the hero from the saddle. The existing JS uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback caller skips dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_KNOCKED), omitting the preferred landing-square RNG draw and dismount effects.

source.branch: During a monster knockback against a mounted hero, uhitm.c:mhitm_knockback stores the knockback direction in u.dx/u.dy and calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_KNOCKED). dismount_steed first calls landing_spot(reason, 0), which orders the preferred square and its two adjacent candidates with rn2(2), then checks viable squares; if a spot is found, it emits the fall message, applies riding-accident damage and wounded legs when unprotected, releases the steed, moves the hero, and restores normal footing.

evidence: Saved queue /home/vtjeng/development/vtjeng/teleport-contest/.cache/latest-saved-combined-queue.json records its v39 evaluation at aed26ac9ec69a4441421005e4110971d52d5eb53, which is an ancestor of accepted Main 85ebf1b2716b3a0f4e0d868d213d9b22f6a30e57. The case had 1/90 screens unmatched, 2873/2890 RNG calls matching, and 89/90 cursors matching. Its RNG mismatch identifies steed.c:landing_spot at line 480.
Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/uhitm.c:5388-5391 (mhitm_knockback) stores the preferred direction in u.dx/u.dy and calls dismount_steed(DISMOUNT_KNOCKED) for a mounted hero defender.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/steed.c:460-566 (landing_spot) creates the preferred adjacent candidate order with rn2(2), then checks movement, known traps, boulders, and distance-based tie breaks. The DISMOUNT_KNOCKED pass starts at i=1 and may fall back to enexto when forceit is set.

Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/steed.c:576-822 (dismount_steed) initializes the first landing spot before clearing u.usteed. DISMOUNT_KNOCKED shares the thrown/fell branch, reports the fall, may apply rn1(10,10) damage and rn1(5,5) wounded-leg duration, then releases the steed and moves the hero before float_down.

The current JS caller js/uhitm.js:7478-7482 records note_unported("steed.c dismount_steed DISMOUNT_KNOCKED") rather than invoking the source callee. The JS helper js/steed.js:752-769 also refuses the DISMOUNT_KNOCKED candidate-order branch; js/steed.js:873-881 refuses the shared dismount reason branch.

Fresh differential .cache/A2-v39-steed-knockoff-diff.log, run from examined commit f2c5e45014e972580219998b20749aa9db9a421b: C made 2,890 RNG calls and JS made 2,882; the first mismatch is call 2,874 at segment 1, step 88, space. C called rn2(2)=0 from landing_spot(steed.c:480), while JS called rn2(4)=0 after skipping the dismount. Both emitted 90 screens; the final boundary differs at row 1, column 5 (C 'f', JS 'w'), and cursors first differ at boundary 90.

The admitted C-first recipe challenges/cases/v39/v39-mounted-steed-knockoff.recipe.session.json (SHA-256 790bf8e88979b4e30d4fb7813de313c8de6b87f250aba1a2f2f9d808efab68f8) wishes a saddled pony, mounts it, then has a hostile Titan attack. C's recorded path reaches the DISMOUNT_KNOCKED branch and retains challenges/cases/v39/v39-mounted-steed-knockoff.session.json (SHA-256 5ee5f9ca6524671540995d4361175b0a74e109b59897ff89df3efaeac7eec484).

The earlier A2 investigation investigations/synthetic/v39/v39-mounted-steed-polymorph-trap.json independently found the same landing_spot helper after mon.c:newcham changes a tame mount. The knockoff case reaches the separate DISMOUNT_KNOCKED entry path and shares the unresolved steed.c implementation family.
